title: fix: distinguish key budgets from wallet payment failures
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Return distinct KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED and INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE codes with the existing 402 status.
- Link key-budget failures to key settings and wallet failures to top-up, including paid-only balance guidance.
- Stop the CLI telling users to top up for exhausted key budgets. No changes to prices, reservations, or deductions.
- Tests: 42 gateway/billing tests and 4 CLI guidance tests; gen typecheck passes.

gist.headline: 402s learn the difference
gist.blurb: A depleted API key budget and an empty wallet now get their own little signposts. Polli has stopped sending everyone to the same jar of honey.
gist.summary: Payment-required responses now distinguish exhausted API key budgets (KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED) from insufficient wallet balances (INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE), while keeping HTTP 402 and directing each case to the relevant settings or top-up flow.
gist.impact: CLI and API users with a spent key budget are guided to key settings, while wallet-balance failures point to top-up guidance, including paid-only balance details.
gist.visual_concept: Depict two friendly, clearly labeled garden paths branching from a retro 402 terminal: one path leads to a tiny key-settings toolbox with an empty key-budget meter, and the other to a warm wallet top-up watering can. Polli, wearing a tiny guide hat and holding a signpost, calmly directs the monitor robot down the correct path; code-plants and flowers make the error-routing metaphor feel helpful rather than alarming.
